nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Ni-Fe-Ce LDH
nodes.procedure: In the three-electrode setup, a clean CC piece served as working electrode, Pt foil as counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl as reference electrode. The electrolyte solution consisted of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, Fe(NO3)3·9H2O and Ce(NO3)3·6H2O. The total concentration of metal salts was maintained at 100 mM, with the initial Ce molar ratio set as 5%. The electrodeposition process was carried out at a constant potential of -0.1 V (vs. Ag/AgCl) for 600 s. After deposition, the resulting Ni-Fe-Ce LDH/CC was washed with DI water and ethanol and dried at 60 °C in vacuum.

nodes.name: Selenization of LDH precursor
nodes.procedure: 0.5 g selenium was evenly laid flat inside a porcelain boat. A piece of Ni-Fe-Ce LDH/CC was placed in the center. The furnace chamber was purged with Ar for 30 min. The furnace was heated to 250 °C with a rate of 5 °C/min and maintained for 2 h. After cooling, the sample was washed with ultrapure water and ethanol and then vacuum dried.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Ni-Fe LDH
nodes.procedure: In the three-electrode setup, a clean CC piece served as the working electrode, a Pt foil as the counter electrode, and a saturated silver chloride electrode (Ag/AgCl) as the reference electrode. The electrolyte solution consisted of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and Fe(NO3)3·9H2O. The total concentration of metal salts was maintained at 100 mM. The electrodeposition process was carried out at a constant potential of -0.1 V (vs. Ag/AgCl) for 600 s. After the deposition, the resulting Ni–Fe LDH/CC was washed several times with DI water and ethanol, followed by drying at 60 °C in a vacuum drying oven.

nodes.name: Selenization of Ni-Fe LDH
nodes.procedure: 0.5 g selenium was evenly laid flat inside a porcelain boat. In the center of this boat, a piece of Ni–Fe LDH/CC was placed. The entire boat was then inserted into a tube furnace. Prior to the heating process, the furnace chamber was purged with highly-purified argon (Ar) for 30 min. After purging, the furnace was heated to 250 °C with a controlled heating rate of 5 °C·min-1 and maintained for 2 h. After the heat treatment, the furnace was allowed to cool down, and the sample was washed with ultrapure water and ethanol, followed by vacuum drying.
